sections.content:
You know spoken discourse markers (*pues*, *vamos*, *bueno*) from C1 Unit 18, evaluative suffixes (*-ito*, *-azo*, *-ucho*) from C1 Unit 22, and aspectual *se* (*leerse*, *comerse*) from C1 Unit 17. Finding your own voice in Spanish means being versatile enough to express the same idea in a formal essay or around a table with friends.

Compare the two registers. In a formal report you write *Tras haber leído el informe entero, concluyo que…*. In relaxed conversation, you say *Pues mira, me leí el informe enterito y, vamos, no está nada mal*. Notice how aspectual *se* (*me leí* + bounded object), a diminutive (*enterito* / *un ratito*) and a conversational marker (*pues*, *vamos*) create warmth, naturalness and ease without losing precision.

The key is conscious choice: use spoken markers and suffixes in conversation, and leave them out of formal prose.

sections.title: The same idea across two registers
rows: *Tras haber leído el ensayo completo, considero que resulta convincente.*
*Pues me leí el ensayo entero y, vamos, me pareció un textazo.*
*Espérame un ratito y afinamos el cierre.* (warmth, not small size)
*Se leyó la novela entera en dos días.* (specific, bounded object)

items.spanish: Pues, la verdad, me leí todo el borrador en una tarde y me pareció buenísimo.
items.english: Well, honestly, I read the whole draft in one afternoon and thought it was great.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo aprendes a expresarte con naturalidad y soltura sin perder autenticidad.
items.english: With time you learn to express yourself with naturalness and ease without losing authenticity.

items.spanish: ¡Menudo exitazo tuvo tu charla de ayer! Vamos, todos salieron encantados.
items.english: What a huge success your talk was yesterday! Honestly, everyone left delighted.

items.spanish: Una hablante versátil sabe cuándo pulir un informe y cuándo charlar un ratito sin rigidez.
items.english: A versatile speaker knows when to polish a report and when to chat for a bit without stiffness.

sections.content: Aspectual *se* (*leerse*, *comerse*, *saberse*) requires a **specific, bounded** direct object (*me leí el libro entero*, never *me leí libros*). And keep spoken markers like *vamos* and evaluative *-azo* in conversation, not in formal reports.
